summary: Phase 7 backend testing complete. 13 new tests for Stripe tiered SaaS + premium gating on /api/public/audit. Results: 11/13 PASS, 2/13 FAIL — both failures root-cause the SAME critical bug in GET /api/payments/checkout/status/{session_id} (returns HTTP 500 instead of handling Stripe 'No such checkout.session' error). Regression: 44/44 prior tests still pass (2 pre-existing slow/flaky tests from iter 4 were deselected and can be re-run on demand). Premium gating on /api/public/audit is fully validated: demo user (subscription_tier='professional') → premium:true, watermark 'AEGIS-Q · PROFESSIONAL · Rapport institutionnel', limits.remaining=999, 5 serial calls from same IP all succeed (rate-limit bypassed). Fresh user without tier → premium:false, watermark starts with 'SAMPLE'. Webhook negative test: empty body + no/bad signature → 400 (not 500).

critical.issue: Returns HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' for any valid session_id because emergentintegrations.StripeCheckout.get_checkout_status() raises stripe._error.InvalidRequestError 'No such checkout.session: cs_test_...' (even for a session that was just created by POST /api/payments/checkout/session — the emergent-proxied Stripe test key does not retain session state between create and retrieve). The handler at server.py:1214 does NOT wrap the call in try/except, so the CheckoutError propagates unhandled and FastAPI returns 500. Impact: (a) polling after a successful checkout is completely broken, (b) the idempotent tier-granting code at server.py:1227-1244 is unreachable for any real payment, (c) frontend /payments/success page cannot display status.

minor.issue: Under 5 concurrent Claude Opus calls from the same premium bearer, 3 of 5 returned upstream 502 'The preview environment is not responding' before hitting the handler. Rate-limit bypass itself is correct (no 429s observed), but concurrent Opus pressure still triggers the ingress timeout. This is the same pre-existing issue documented in iter 4 — not Phase 7 specific.
Returns 403 'Not authenticated' (FastAPI HTTPBearer default) instead of 401. Test accepts both; consumers expecting 401 per spec may need adjustment.

action_items: CRITICAL: Wrap stripe_checkout.get_checkout_status() in get_checkout_status (server.py:1214) with try/except CheckoutError. Either (a) return HTTP 502 with French detail + preserve DB-cached status so the frontend can still show 'pending', OR (b) if sk_test_emergent genuinely can't retrieve sessions, fall back to returning the DB-cached payment_status (initiated/pending) and rely on the webhook for the real status transition. Current 500 breaks all /payments/success polling.

Investigate why emergent-proxied sk_test_emergent creates session IDs that cannot be retrieved via the Stripe REST API. Possibly the integration needs a different api_key pair for retrieval vs creation, or Stripe events need to be consumed via webhook only.
Consider returning 401 (not 403) for missing Bearer token on POST /api/payments/checkout/session for consistency with spec (minor).
Carry-over from iter 4: harden public_audit against concurrent Opus 502s; add retry/backoff.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1214 calls `await stripe_checkout.get_checkout_status(session_id)` with NO try/except — any Stripe SDK error (session not found, network, rate-limited) becomes an unhandled 500. This is the root cause of both Phase 7 failures and the single biggest correctness issue in Phase 7.

server.py is now ~1774 lines (+240 since iter 4). Stripe payments block (L1104-1286), public audit (L1294+), functions, auth, and entities all live in one file. Split into auth.py, payments.py, public_audit.py is overdue.

webhook_url is recomputed from request.base_url inside EVERY create_checkout_session / get_checkout_status / stripe_webhook call — this builds a fresh StripeCheckout client each request with no connection reuse. Move StripeCheckout instantiation to module scope or FastAPI startup with a configurable WEBHOOK_URL env var.

PAYMENT_PACKAGES pricing is hardcoded (L1110-1113). This is correct for security (never trust frontend prices), but the comment says 'enterprise is contact-sales' while the frontend brochure may still try to POST package_id='enterprise' — no explicit rejection test. Consider adding `raise 400 'Contact sales'` for the enterprise path.

CheckoutSessionBody.origin_url has no URL scheme validation — a malicious client can pass 'javascript:' or a phishing domain and the success_url / cancel_url will embed it. Add AnyHttpUrl validation and/or allowlist of trusted origins.

Tier-granting logic (L1234-1244) is inside the GET /status handler rather than the webhook handler. This means tier upgrades only happen when the USER polls /status after returning from Stripe — if they close the tab, the tier is never granted despite a successful payment. The webhook already receives the session_id (L1274) but does NOT call db.users.update_one to grant the tier. Duplicate this logic into stripe_webhook for at-least-once delivery.
payment_transactions collection has no unique index on session_id — two concurrent checkout creations for the same user could theoretically race (unlikely but not prevented).

Premium detection in public_audit (L1377-1391) silently swallows ANY JWT decode exception (`except Exception: pass`). A genuinely malformed Authorization header from a legitimate premium user will silently fall back to anonymous rate-limited mode. Log at DEBUG level at minimum so we can debug premium users getting 429s.

_client_ip uses request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for').split(',')[0] — X-Forwarded-For is untrusted from the client; use request.headers.get('x-real-ip') or the ingress-sanctioned header only, or rate-limit bypass becomes trivially spoofable by setting X-Forwarded-For.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 7 tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_phase7_payments.py (separate from backend_test.py intentionally — keeps Stripe-coupled tests isolable). The 2 failing tests (TestCheckoutStatus::test_status_valid_session, TestPaymentTxPersistence::test_tx_row_created) will PASS once server.py:1214 is wrapped in try/except CheckoutError returning an appropriate non-500 response. To reproduce: authenticate as demo@, POST a checkout session, then GET its status — observe 500 in response + `stripe._error.InvalidRequestError: No such checkout.session` in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. Premium gating is fully working and its 3 tests pass reliably when called SERIALLY (as the suite does). Webhook negative tests correctly return 400 — no positive webhook test is feasible without Stripe CLI. Regression: invoke `pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py --deselect backend/tests/backend_test.py::TestPublicAudit::test_rate_limit_serial_same_ip -k 'not test_market_prices_authenticated'` to reproduce the 44/44. The 2 deselected tests are pre-existing slow (rate-limit, 4x Opus) and pre-existing flaky (CoinGecko usd=0) from iter 4 — not Phase 7 regressions.
rca of the issue: Both failing Phase 7 tests share one root cause: server.py line 1214 (`status = await stripe_checkout.get_checkout_status(session_id)`) is not wrapped in try/except. The emergentintegrations library raises CheckoutError wrapping the underlying stripe._error.InvalidRequestError('No such checkout.session') because the emergent-proxied sk_test_emergent key creates sessions whose IDs are not retrievable via the standard Stripe retrieval API (hypothesis: the proxy uses different accounts for create vs retrieve, or sessions auto-expire immediately). Because CheckoutError inherits from Exception (not HTTPException), FastAPI converts it to a generic 500 Internal Server Error. Mitigation: wrap in try/except CheckoutError and (a) if Stripe fetch fails, return the DB-cached row as-is (status='initiated', payment_status='pending'); (b) log the underlying Stripe error at WARNING. This also fixes the currently-unreachable tier-granting code path if the webhook path is also hardened (see code-review comment on tier-granting duplication). Reproduction steps: (1) login demo@, (2) POST /api/payments/checkout/session {package_id:'starter', origin_url:'...'}, (3) GET /api/payments/checkout/status/{returned_session_id} → observe 500. Backend log shows 'No such checkout.session: cs_test_...'.
